result.topic_en: Gauss derives a finite product identity for (1+y)(1+x^2y)...(1+x^{n-1}y) for odd n and, letting n go to infinity, obtains the Jacobi triple product form of the theta series.
result.transcription:
Math. 25 \quad (87) [-77-] 36

muß[?] noch sein[?]
$(1+y)(1+xxy)(1+x^4y)\cdots(1+x^{n-1}y)$
Da nun[?]
$B=\frac{1-x^{n+3}}{1-xx}\cdot\frac{1-x^{n+5}}{1-x^4}\cdot\frac{1-x^{n+7}}{1-x^6}\cdots\frac{1-x^{2n}}{1-x^{n-1}}\cdot\frac{x^{\frac14nn-n+\frac34}}{x^{\frac12nn-n+\frac12}\cdot x^{\frac14}}y^{\frac12(n-1)}y^{\frac12}$
$=\frac{1-x^{n+3}}{1-xx}\cdots\frac{1-x^{2n}}{1-x^{n-1}}\cdot\frac{y^{\frac12n}}{x^{\frac14nn}}$
So ergibt das erste Theorem folgendes 3^{te}
Wenn n ungerades n[?] ist
$x^{\frac14}(y^{\frac12}+y^{-\frac12})+\frac{1-x^{n-1}}{1-x^{n+3}}\cdot x^{\frac94}(y^{\frac32}+y^{-\frac32})+\frac{1-x^{n-1}}{1-x^{n+3}}x^{\frac{25}{4}}(y^{\frac52}+y^{-\frac52})+\text{etc}$
$=x^{\frac14}(y^{\frac12}+y^{-\frac12})(1+xxy)(1+x^4y)(1+x^6y)\cdots(1+x^{n-1}y)$
$\times(1+\frac{xx}{y})(1+\frac{x^4}{y})(1+\frac{x^6}{y})\cdots(1+\frac{x^{n-1}}{y})$
$\times\frac{1-xx}{1-x^{n+3}}\cdot\frac{1-x^4}{1-x^{n+5}}\cdot\frac{1-x^6}{1-x^{n+7}}\cdots\frac{1-x^{n-1}}{1-x^{2n}}$

4.
Wenn man n ins unendliche wachsen läßt, so verwandeln sich die Reihen und Producte des dritten u. 2^{ten}[?] Theorems in unendliche Reihen u. Producte. In dieser Gestalt ist das 4^{te} Theorem
$1+x(y+\frac1y)+x^4(yy+\frac1{yy})+x^9(y^3+\frac1{y^3})+\text{etc. in inf.}$
$=(1+xy)(1+\frac xy)(1+x^3y)(1+\frac{x^3}{y})(1+x^5y)(1+\frac{x^5}{y})\cdots\text{in inf}$
$\times(1-xx)(1-x^4)(1-x^6)(1-x^8)\cdots$

methods.what: Simplification of the coefficient B (q-binomial-type quotient) for odd n
Third theorem: finite product identity (finite form of triple product) for odd n
Fourth theorem: Jacobi triple product identity obtained as limit n→∞
